summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for evaluation of diarrhea, weight loss, and malaise. She was found to have severe neutropenia, acute kidney injury, and non-gap metabolic acidosis. Infectious workup including stool, blood, and urine cultures was negative, and CMV viral load was undetectable. An EGD and colonoscopy revealed histologic evidence of ischemic colitis, likely due to mycophenolate mofetil, prompting a switch to myfortic with rapid improvement in diarrhea. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted to improve low white blood cell counts, and tacrolimus was uptitrated to 3 mg twice daily. She was started on megace for appetite stimulation and zinc for deficiency, leading to weight gain from 50.8 kg to 54.9 kg. Her kidney function improved with hydration, and she was discharged on stable medications with plans for close outpatient follow-up, including weekly CMV monitoring and transplant clinic visit.
